ArticleDelivery.description:
The article Tribune Desk sends to your webhook when an editor clicks "Send to CMS".

Fields marked as omitted are absent from the body, not null, when they do not apply.
New fields may be added in a minor version; ignore the ones you do not know.

ai_provenance.description: Level 3 (full content). AI provenance statement, also embedded in `html`; null when the newsroom turned marking off.

alternative_titles.description: Optional (editorial extras). Other headline proposals; may be empty.
alternative_titles.title: Alternative Titles

article_id.description: Level 1 (receive article). Tribune Desk id of the article. Repeated sends of the same article carry the same id: update the post you created the first time.
article_id.title: Article Id

author.description: Level 3 (full content). Who ordered the article. Use it as the post author when `sent_by` cannot be matched.

backlink_sources.description: Level 3 (full content). Older articles that should link to this one. Omitted = leave existing links alone; an empty list = no article should link here.
backlink_sources.title: Backlink Sources

custom_content.description: Optional (editorial extras). Extra text blocks defined by the newsroom.
custom_content.title: Custom Content

evergreen.description: Level 3 (full content). True when the article stays current (not tied to news).
evergreen.title: Evergreen

excerpt.description: Level 1 (receive article). A short summary of the article for the post excerpt (the chosen meta description); null when there is none.
excerpt.title: Excerpt

facebook_teaser.description: Optional (editorial extras). The chosen teaser for Facebook.
facebook_teaser.title: Facebook Teaser

facebook_teasers.description: Optional (editorial extras). All teaser proposals for Facebook.
facebook_teasers.title: Facebook Teasers

facebook_title.description: Optional (editorial extras). The chosen title for Facebook. Use it only on Facebook, not as the post title.
facebook_title.title: Facebook Title

facebook_titles.description: Optional (editorial extras). All title proposals for Facebook.
facebook_titles.title: Facebook Titles

featured_image.description: Level 1 (receive article). The main image: the same object as the first entry of `generated_images`; null when the article has no images.

focus_keyphrase.description: Level 3 (full content). The focus keyphrase for SEO.
focus_keyphrase.title: Focus Keyphrase

generated_images.description: Level 3 (full content). Images made for the article; the first one is the main image.
generated_images.title: Generated Images

html.description: Level 1 (receive article). The article body as HTML, without the headline. Internal links are already resolved (see `internal_links`).
html.title: Html

internal_links.description: Level 3 (full content). Links to other articles of the newsroom placed in `html`.
internal_links.title: Internal Links

language.description: Level 1 (receive article). The newsroom's writing language (e.g. `pl`). Omitted when not set.

link_placeholder_prefix.description: Level 3 (full content). Every link in `html` to an article that has no address in your CMS yet is `link_placeholder_prefix` followed by that article's `article_id`. Replace it with your address of that article, or keep only the link text. Do not hard-code the prefix.
link_placeholder_prefix.title: Link Placeholder Prefix

meta_description.description: Level 3 (full content). The chosen meta description.
meta_description.title: Meta Description

metadata.description: Level 1 (receive article). Where the article comes from.

org_code.description: Level 1 (receive article). The newsroom's code in Tribune Desk.
org_code.title: Org Code

raw_facts.description: Optional (editorial extras). Facts the article was written from, one per line.
raw_facts.title: Raw Facts

reel_captions.description: Optional (editorial extras). Proposed captions for reels.
reel_captions.title: Reel Captions

sent_at.description: Level 1 (receive article). When this send was made (ISO 8601).
sent_at.title: Sent At

sent_by.description: Level 3 (full content). Who clicked "Send to CMS"; null for automatic sends.

seo_title.description: Level 3 (full content). The chosen SEO title.
seo_title.title: Seo Title

title.description: Level 1 (receive article). The article's headline. Not repeated in `html`.
title.title: Title

topic.description: Optional (editorial extras). The topic the article was written on.
topic.title: Topic

twitter_posts.description: Optional (editorial extras). Proposed posts for X.
twitter_posts.title: Twitter Posts

info.description:
Contract between a CMS and Tribune Desk. The CMS is the client: it polls changes with a cursor (`GET /changes`) and sends its own.

**Authentication:** `Authorization: Bearer tdcms_...`. A super admin issues the token for one organization with scopes `media:read`, `media:write`, `settings:read`, `settings:write`, `backfill:write`, `articles:read`, `articles:write`.

**Limits:** 600 requests per minute per token (`429` with `Retry-After`).

**Errors:** every error of every route has the body `ApiError` (`code`, `message`, `retry_after`).

Operations marked `x-status: planned` require their scope but answer `501 not_implemented`.
info.title: Tribune Desk CMS API

get.description: Read mode: the sends your CMS has not reported a result for yet, oldest first, up to 100 per page. Use it after `410 cursor_expired` on `GET /changes` when your token has no `media:write` for `POST /resync`: handle these sends, then poll `GET /changes` again without a cursor. A send replaced by a newer send of the same article is not listed.

403.description: `forbidden`: the token lacks the scope of this route.

422.description: `validation_error`: the request does not match the schema.

429.description: `rate_limited`: retry after `retry_after` seconds (the `Retry-After` header carries the same whole number of seconds).

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying; the same as `retry_after`.
Whole seconds to wait before retrying; the same as `retry_after`.

get.summary: List sends waiting for a result (read mode)

post.description: Level 2 (link back): tell Tribune Desk the public address of posts made from delivered articles, 1 to 100 per request. Tribune Desk shows the link to the editor and uses the article as a target of internal links. Each item gets its own status; a bad item does not fail the others. Repeating an item with the same address changes nothing.

403.description: `forbidden`: the token lacks the scope of this route.

post.description: Read mode: the body your webhook would answer with, plus `delivery_id` and `error` (`ArticleResultReport`). Tribune Desk stores `social_queue_exclude`, `permalink`, `cms_post_id` and `edit_url` and marks the send as delivered; with `error` it marks the send as failed and stores nothing else. Unlike a webhook answer, this request is validated: a field of the wrong type gives `422 validation_error`. A field of the right type that is not stored (an `edit_url` that is not `http(s)`, a `permalink` that is not a public address) is listed in `ignored_fields`. post.description: Up to 100 items, downloaded later at their own pace; `cms_media_id` is any text of yours. `ok`: accepted; `known`: already received. Both carry `asset_id` once the file exists in Tribune Desk. An accepted item has no file yet: the pair appears after the import, and until then `POST /media/fields`, `POST /media/deletions` and `POST /resync` treat the id as unknown. A refusal is not remembered: send the item again after the settings change. New files are not subject to `mass_change_threshold`; initial `fields` only help describe the file (see the schema). `409 state_conflict` when the integration or the media library is not enabled.

post.description: Up to 100 items, each `cms_media_id` once. The file is marked as missing from the CMS and is no longer suggested to editors, whatever the settings say; the mark is set to `deleted_at`. With `cms_deletion_trashes_in_td` the file also goes to the trash; nothing is ever deleted permanently. `ok`: recorded. `known`: this deletion was already recorded. `unknown`: no such file in this organization yet; a file sent with `POST /media` and not imported yet answers this too, so report it again later. Moves to the trash count towards `mass_change_threshold` in the same 60-minute run as field changes; past it the file only gets the mark and the item answers `ok` with `reason: threshold`. That is final: repeating answers `known` and does not trash it. `held_batch_id` stays `null`: nothing waits for a decision. A trash caused here can also produce a `deleted` change in `GET /changes` when `td_deletion_marks_in_cms` is on; ignore it for a file you no longer have. post.description: Two forms. Preview: upload the CMS state, up to 100 items per request, in pages (`is_last` closes the upload), for either direction; nothing changes and the answer carries the number of differences. Confirm: `{resync_id, confirm: true}` applies a `ready` preview within 24 hours and returns the cursor to resume `/changes` from. The chosen direction wins. Resync covers only paired files; it does not restore new files or deletions - those need `POST /media/push-existing`. `409 state_conflict`: the integration is not enabled for the organization, a preview with more than 50000 differences, a page sent to a closed or expired session or with a different direction than its first page, or confirming a preview that is not `ready` or has expired, or a session started before the integration was re-enabled (run a new resync). Repeating the confirmation of an applied or held resync changes nothing and gives the same answer. Only fields enabled in the settings for the direction are compared and applied. Over `mass_change_threshold` differences the confirmation changes nothing and answers `status: held` with `held_batch_id` and the cursor: decide with `POST /held/{id}/decision`.

post.description:
Sent when an editor clicks "Send to CMS" (or a newsroom widget sends the article). Tribune Desk makes a `POST` with a JSON body to the webhook address set for the organization.

**Signature:** every request carries `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature` as defined by Standard Webhooks: HMAC-SHA256 of `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{body}`, keyed with the base64-decoded secret, as `v1,<base64>`. Two active secrets give two space-separated signatures; any match is valid. Reject a timestamp more than 5 minutes from your clock. `webhook-id` is the same for every attempt of one send. The signature is the only proof that a request comes from Tribune Desk. An organization without a signing secret (`whsec_...`, issued by a super admin) gets no deliveries, so a request without these headers is not from Tribune Desk.

**Headers:** `X-Delivery-Id` stays the same for every attempt of one send, so you can drop duplicates; `X-Delivery-Attempt` is the attempt number, starting at 1. `User-Agent` is `ArticleWriter/2`. Deliveries come from no fixed IP address: the signature, not the address, proves the sender.

**Your answer:** any `2xx` means delivered. Answer within 30 seconds.

**Retries:** after a network error, a timeout, `5xx` or `408, 425, 429`, Tribune Desk tries again after 2, 10, 30, 120, 360, 840 minutes. Any other status (another `4xx`, or a `3xx`: redirects are not followed) ends the send at once.

**Idempotency:** the same article comes again with the same `article_id` when it is resent or edited: update the post you created the first time, do not create a second one.

**Order:** a newer send of the same article cancels the pending retries of an older one, and every attempt carries the current state of the article. An attempt of an older send that was already on its way can still arrive after a newer one: skip a body whose `sent_at` is older than the `sent_at` you last applied for that `article_id`.

parameters.description: Id of the send, the same for every attempt (Standard Webhooks).
parameters.name: webhook-id

parameters.description: Unix time of this attempt, in seconds.
parameters.name: webhook-timestamp

200.description: Delivered. Any `2xx` counts; the body is optional.

3XX.description: Not delivered; redirects are not followed, the send ends.

4XX.description: Not delivered. `408, 425, 429` are retried; any other `4xx` ends the send at once (for example a failed signature check or an unknown organization).
